text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former military ruler retired General Ibrahim Babangida objects to court summons to testify in a libel suit.
- Demand for foreign exchange rises by $4 million at weekly auction.
- Fourteen die in police female soccer team road crash.
- A $100 million World Bank loan portfolio to Nigeria has been left undisbursed for several years, Bank officials say.
- President of Nigerian Stock Exchange Pascal Dozie urges government to resume privatisation of public enterprises.
- Decree to set up commodity exchange could be signed by military ruler General Sani Abacha by month end, sources say.
- Petroleum Trust Fund, which oversees money made by government from increase in pump prices, to fund a master study for fisheries development, says director of fisheries.
